clue.text: Avoid pigpen or strange child's plaything

parts.note: to skip something is to avoid or miss it out

indicators.note: something strange is odd or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A child gives a muddy pigsty a wide berth on the way to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Avoid' looks like an instruction to the child, but it supplies the opening word; 'strange' rearranges the pigpen letters to finish the toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipping rope is a simple toy children jump over in playground games.

clue.text: One can't go and do it

definitions.text: One can't go and do it

parts.words: One can't go and do it
parts.note: someone who cannot leave has no choice but to remain where they are

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark about something a person unable to leave must still do.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the action: if you cannot go, what you do is remain.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay means to remain in place, the opposite of going away.

clue.text: Coastal batting support

parts.note: a cricket side that is batting is said to be 'in'
to shore something up is to prop or support it

explanation.surface: A cricket team batting by the sea, with some kind of backing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the team currently batting is 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inshore waters lie close to the coast, so the word describes something near the seaside.

clue.text: Initially police called to minor accident

indicators.note: says only the opening letter of the word police is used

explanation.surface: Police are summoned to the scene of a small road incident.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a minor crash, especially a car bump.
explanation.definitionFit: A prang is informal British slang for a small collision involving a vehicle.

clue.text: Wanderers cooking damson

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters of damson are reworked

explanation.surface: Travellers preparing a plum-based dish on their way.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomads are people who roam from place to place with no fixed home.

clue.text: Sweet drink sailors rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the sailors are written backwards

parts.note: AB (able-bodied seaman) is a sailor, so two sailors are AB twice

explanation.surface: Seamen turn down a sugary cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum baba is a dessert of yeast cake soaked in rum syrup.

clue.text: Swing a camera to show

parts.note: to pan is to swing a camera horizontally to follow a scene

explanation.surface: Instructions to a camera operator filming a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: A panto (pantomime) is a British family Christmas stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Panto is short for pantomime, a festive comic theatre entertainment.

clue.text: Sweet affectionate insect

explanation.surface: A description of a lovable little bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' reads as an adjective describing the insect, but it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondant is a soft sugary confection, so it is a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Unable to cope away from land

definitions.meaning: being ... idiomatically means being confused and lost

explanation.surface: A sailor overwhelmed far out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both an idiom for bewilderment and a literal description of a ship's position offshore.

clue.text: Tome men reprint? No, just a reminder

indicators.note: reprinting sets the letters again, so tome men are rearranged

explanation.surface: Publishers ask whether a big book needs a new edition, then decide a keepsake will do.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a souvenir kept to recall a person or event.

clue.text: Unprepared sparkler could be good in Durham

definitions.meaning: a person who is good-hearted beneath rough manners, a type associated with gritty northern places

explanation.surface: An uncut gem that might be found good in a northern English city.
explanation.walkthrough: Durham is a former coal-mining city in north-east England, evoking plain-spoken, rough-edged folk.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both an uncut gem and a kind-hearted person lacking polish.

clue.text: Satisfy monkey consuming greens

indicators.note: consuming means eating, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: ape is to mimic, the sense of monkey as a verb, and also a primate

explanation.surface: Feeding vegetables to a primate to keep it happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' tells you the primate swallows the vegetables, which sit just after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To appease someone is to pacify them by giving them what they demand.

clue.text: Make hole in jetty adjoining church

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: Damage to a landing stage next to a seaside church.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to puncture or bore through something.

clue.text: Vigorously study British city

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
Rio de Janeiro is a city

explanation.surface: Someone energetically researching a UK city.
explanation.definitionFit: Con brio is a musical direction meaning with spirit and energy.

clue.text: Automobile (French) good like a diamond!

definitions.note: the answer is a noun; a diamond is made of it, so the definition describes it by example

parts.note: bon is French for good, as the bracketed (French) signals

explanation.surface: A French car praised as brilliant as a gem.
explanation.walkthrough: '(French)' tells you to put 'good' into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamond is a crystalline form of the element carbon.

clue.text: Country has it in intellect

indicators.note: in says the word it goes inside the other piece

explanation.surface: A nation boasting of its brainpower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is only a link here; 'in' is what places the little word inside the word for intellect.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain is the island nation of England, Scotland and Wales.

clue.text: Soldier insects, big ones

explanation.surface: Large soldier ants, a caste that guards the colony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier insects' looks like the ant caste, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Giants are huge beings, so they are notably large ones.

clue.text: A tensile soil mixture producing scented unguent

indicators.note: a mixture blends things, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Stretchy earth is blended to produce a fragrant ointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Essential oils are fragrant plant extracts used in perfume and aromatherapy ointments.

clue.text: Put away, but decays round start of Easter

indicators.note: turned round, so the word for decays is written backwards
takes just the opening letter of the word Easter

explanation.surface: Hide chocolate eggs, since they spoil around Easter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a container signal, but here it turns the word for decays back to front, giving STOR before the E.
explanation.definitionFit: To store something is to keep it aside for later.

clue.text: Further down a cow?

definitions.meaning: a cow lows, i.e. moos, so it is something that lows

explanation.surface: A cow seen further down the field.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is pronounced to rhyme with 'slower': one who lows, a moo-er.
explanation.definitionFit: Lower is the comparative of low, and a whimsical noun for a mooing animal.

clue.text: In this place, but in another era

indicators.note: in signals the answer sits within the letters of another era

explanation.surface: Being in this very spot, but living in a different age.
explanation.definitionFit: Here means at or in this location.

clue.text: Managed, after most of game, to get ornamental pouch

indicators.note: after places the word for managed after the other piece
most of drops the last letter of the word for game

explanation.surface: Someone handles the hunting season to win a decorative bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the final letter of the game word. A sporran is the pouch worn in front of a Scottish kilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporran is a decorative purse hanging from the belt of Highland dress.

clue.text: We hear the moan of Moby-Dick

indicators.note: says we are told how a word sounds rather than how it is written

parts.note: a wail is a moan or cry

explanation.surface: Listening to the mournful cry of Melville's great beast.
explanation.definitionFit: Moby-Dick is the white sperm whale in Herman Melville's novel, so an example of the answer.

clue.text: Protestation about church vessel

parts.note: a monstrance is a vessel used to display the host in Catholic churches

explanation.surface: A complaint concerning some piece of church plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A remonstrance is a formal protest or objection.
